hook_text: It is January. Polokwane is sweating at thirty degrees. A school in Norway is under snow. Why?
clip_script: A video call between Polokwane and Norway in January. In Limpopo, learners are in short sleeves. In Norway, children are in thick jackets and it is dark by mid-afternoon. Near the equator, the sun's rays hit the Earth almost straight on, so it is hot. Near the poles, the rays come in at a low slant and spread out, so it is cold. In between, the climate is mild. In July, the seasons swap.
visual_style: Whiteboard globe with sunlight arrows hitting the equator straight on and the poles at a slant, then two world maps coloured red, yellow and blue for January and July.
mood: Bright and curious, with a playful contrast between heat and snow.
pacing: A quick call, a slow explanation with the torch and globe, then map reading step by step.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find three places on the January map that are hot while South Africa is hot too.
